title.narrative: Modernization of Irrigation Techniques to Improve the Livelihoods of Smallholder Farmers in Upper Egypt

description.narrative: The project aims to improve water efficiency through designing modern irrigation systems in Assiut, Sohag, and Qena in Egypt as Phase 1. These systems are designed to optimize water efficiency, increase agricultural productivity, and strengthen the resilience of small tenure holders. Leveraging UN-Habitat's expertise from the "Developing Irrigation Associations for On-Farm Water Management Project" in Afghanistan and “Increasing Climate Change Resilience in Rural Damascus” in Syria, the project aims at introducing water efficient modern irrigation techniques in addition to land consolidation across 650 feddans. Key activities include conducting topographical surveys and designing water efficient irrigation networks, land use consolidation, and establishing 225 Field Schools for participatory extension and climate-smart training. The project also provides comprehensive training on efficient water use and management, irrigation operation, and value chain standards while strengthening public-private-community partnerships and market linkages. These efforts aim to enhance water productivity, agricultural output, and livelihoods for smallholder communities in Upper Egypt. UN-Habitat is nominated by FAO to be the main coordinator for the activities that will have cross contributions from FAO and relevant local authorities for the agriculture activities. FAO nomination was mainly based on UN-Habitat’s relevant previous experience in water sector, urban-rural linkages in addition to its experience in Egypt in land
